I think about this a lot and was curious to see your guy's opinions. I'm personally a fan of a unique aesthetic i.e. Kirby and the Rainbow Curse, Borderlands, LoZ Wind Waker, but a lot of people seem to like realism a lot more.

So, realism or a unique style, and why?
What's your thoughts on unique aesthetics vs realistic graphics in video games? Which do you like more? Why?
It depends on the game. There is no "best" art style. Games like The Last of Us wouldn't look good in a borderlands style and games like Kirby wouldn't be the same if they used realism.
Yea for sure, there's definitely a place for each.
And on top of this some games don't need super high-def graphics if the gameplay is spot-on. I'm not talking about resolution or frame rate here, but sometimes simple graphics are the answer.
Yeah it depends, I like dishonoured as well as the last of us
I personally prefer games with more cartoony art stlyes like Team Fortress 2 as opposed to the more realistic colorless style shown in games like Fallout 3 or Call of Duty.

I think the "colorless style" was a sort of fad back then. More games now are starting to have better color palettes than they did before, but still retaining that "realistic" sort of look. Like compare GTA V to IV, or Fallout 4 to 3. Games seems to be shifting away from that "HD brown filter."
I think it had something to do with hardware/development limitations, if you blend all of the textures under the same color pallet you can't really tell how low-res and shitty they are.

Well, the muddy-brown art style in earlier games like HL2, Quake, and Fallout were meant to set the game's mood, as they were all set in wasteland/apocalyptic environments.

It wasn't until later when using browns and greys became synonymous with "realism" in games.

I think that more cartoony and unique styles make for more compelling games. For example at E3 there were games like Firewatch and Dreams and Cuphead which all grabbed my attention way quicker than the most of the bland, gritty, realistic games did because of their unique and IMO beautiful graphics.

While the issue of graphics is a mostly subjective issue, I prefer a unique style.

TF2's cartoony art, Awesomenaut's Saturday morning cartoon style, and Shovel Knight's retro appeal all help make those games stand out.

And games with realistic graphics risk the chance of entering the uncanny valley

I slightly prefer games with a unique art style, because it makes them timeless. See the Wii U for example (or a lot of other, old Nintendo hits). It can't keep up with the PS4 or X1 graphics wise, but check the art style of some games... Super Mario 3D world, Pikmin 3, Splatoon, Yoshi's Woolly World for example.. They're not awesome graphics wise because of their high-res textures and stuff, but they look awesome because of their art and that also makes them timeless. You can always look back at older games and appreciate their art style, but I doubt you still think SWAT looks awesome, and that's newer than some Nintendo classics

Exactly, aging is my main gripe with realistic graphics. My friend had an interesting point on this when discussing it irl though. He said, "You should play realistic games at release if that's the case, because it's the only time you'll really appreciate their visuals." Interesting thought.

But yea, Splatoon is one of my favorite games ever visually, and maybe gameplay wise too. Haven't tried Pikmin 3 yet, definitely on the to-do list though.

For me attempts at realism either look bad because they haven't been pulled off successfully or good because real life has been emulated to a believable degree. There's little room for subjectivity when it comes to aesthetics at that point, it either looks good because it looks believably real or it doesn't because it isn't. The opposite is true for a unique aesthetic, it's more subjective as to whether it'll be a style I find appealing because there's no real perfect art style.

If I find a game with an art style that I like then I generally prefer how it looks to attempts at realism.

Here's the thing, no matter how "realistic" a games graphics are, they're still going to follow a visual style. This is evident everywhere outside of gaming. Every day people watch movies filmed with real people in real life that have a visual tone, but it's treated via color grading and set dressing. So, for me, I'm more interested in the bigger picture. Are you composing your universe in such a way as to convey the intended feelings correctly? Hotline Miami, The Wolf Among Us, Skyrim/Fallout, and TF2-these are all games that dress the set appropriately and really get me into the intended mood. The text, the music, the environment, everything fits the narrative. That's what makes a good game for me, not their choice of aesthetics.

Although, I can definitely dig some unique art. Cuphead is going to be a treat to look at.

I used to be really for unique aesthetics, since it would give something that makes games stand out. But the main reason for me to used to think that was, because I didn't consider anything realistic looking. To my opinion gaming has always looked low quality. Up untill I saw an UE4 demo, the first engine that makes things look realistic according to my standards.

However, why not both?

I think just like there's all different styles of movies there should be all different kinds of games : realistic, gritty, noir, cartoony, exaggerated. We shouldn't be trying to figure out which is best but exploring all the unique styles and dreaming up new ones.

Yea it's definitely a matter of opinion, I guess I worded the post poorly, didn't mean to make it seem as if there's a clear "better" style. I agree though, I love to see variety visually in games, and I feel like things are really getting interesting lately with games like Yoshis Wooly World and Cuphead.

I'd just like to say I think it's awesome a topic like this one can get a bit of traction here, and lead to actual thoughtful discussion. There's uh, certain gaming communities where this would be buried by jokes. This is a great community, let's keep it that way :)

I feel like games with more cartoon-ish graphics are generally more fun

realistic looking games always seem to dark and down for my taste

it all depends on taste tho

It depends on the game, I like games with a well realized art style. It's a lot easier to do a consistent cartoon or stylized art than to do good realistic stuff. Graphical fidelity doesn't mean shit if you can't use it properly.

It's easy to be blown away by new "photo-realistic" technologies that come out. They're always amazing sights to behold, but a game with a unique art style will more than like stand the test of time a lot better.

I believe it also vastly depends on the intended tone and setting of the game. I'm not really picky either way.

I agree with you on the unique aesthetic, I find they last the test of time more and help create a more interesting world. While realism has its merits with trying to tie it to reality or authenticity of certain weapons and/or events.
It depends on what your game is. Realism works for some games, while for others a unique aesthetic is better. But I do like unique aesthetics a lot. Mirror's Edge, Super Mario, etc.

Depends on the game. If you take Borderlands and slap a realustic skin on it, you get Rage. It didn't work. A reaslistic Tiny Tina would be awful.

OTOH I don't think a hyper stylized Skyrim or Fallout would work.

Personally I believe that in some cases, great 'style' and 'themes' is more important than great animations. The best example would be Team ico's games, such as Ico, Shadow of the Colossus, and their upcoming - the last guardian. Still breathtaking despite having outdated graphics for this time.

It can always be argued that what's "best" depends on the kind of game, or whatever the developers envision it to be.

While that's probably the cop-out answer, I feel-- in reality-- a unique aesthetic will always trump one that's going for realism. Uniqueness is somewhat a timeless thing, while "realism" can only really be called that way up until the point where aesthetic begins to look dated.
